passage.label: Ali 'Imran — Limited harm of disbelievers; abasement stamped upon them except rope from Allah and rope from people; wrath and poverty earned through disbelief, killing prophets, transgression; among People of Book an upright community reciting ayat at night prostrating; believing in Allah and Last Day enjoining good forbidding evil hastening to good deeds among righteous; whatever good they do never denied; Allah knows muttaqin

arabicExcerpts.text: لَن يَضُرُّوكُمۡ إِلَّآ أَذٗىۖ وَإِن يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ يُوَلُّوكُمُ ٱلۡأَدۡبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ

ضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ أَيۡنَ مَا ثُقِفُوٓاْ إِلَّا بِحَبۡلٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَحَبۡلٖ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
۞لَيۡسُواْ سَوَآءٗۗ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أُمَّةٞ قَآئِمَةٞ يَتۡلُونَ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَهُمۡ يَسۡجُدُونَ
يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُسَٰرِعُونَ فِي ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ
وَمَا يَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ فَلَن يُكۡفَرُوهُۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ

mainSubject.label: Limited capacity of hostile factions to harm believers; abasement (dhillah) and destitution (maskanah) imposed upon them except through divine or human covenant; divine wrath earned through systematic disbelief, unjust killing of prophets, and habitual transgression; recognition of an upright community (ummah qaimah) among People of the Book who recite ayat at night, prostrate, believe in Allah and Last Day, enjoin good, forbid evil, hasten to good deeds; their righteousness acknowledged; no good deed of theirs will be denied; Allah's knowledge of the muttaqin

notes: Pass A Imran passage 13/16. Continues Ahl al-Kitab discourse from p12. Introduces dual-rope exception (habl min Allah + habl min al-nas) to universal abasement. Ummah qaimah (3:113-114) provides positive model within Ahl al-Kitab paralleling khayra ummah (3:110). Amr/nahy appears again confirming its cross-communal moral significance.
